mainTopic: רבי יוחנן's keys in ה׳'s hand, and the opinions on when to start mentioning rain in davening, with their sources
overview: This amud finishes רבי יוחנן's list of keys that ה׳ keeps for Himself, with a verse for the key of תחיית המתים. The scholars of ארץ ישראל add a key of פרנסה, and the גמרא explains that for רבי יוחנן rain already includes פרנסה. Then the גמרא asks where רבי אליעזר learns that we start mentioning rain on the first יום טוב of סוכות: from לולב, which would mean starting by day, or from ניסוך המים, which would mean starting the night before. רבי אבהו answers that it is from לולב, and a ברייתא shows this. In that ברייתא, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue whether mentioning rain on סוכות is fitting, since rain on סוכות is a curse. רבי אליעזר answers that mentioning rain is only praise, like mentioning תחיית המתים. The גמרא answers for רבי יהושע: rain is not a blessing at every time, as a משנה about rain after ניסן shows. Finally, the גמרא explains why רבי יהודה בן בתירה starts on the second day and רבי עקיבא on the sixth day. Both base it on a hint in the תורה to ניסוך המים.

steps.title: Finishing the childbirth proof and proving the key of resurrection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the verse that proves the key of childbirth. Then it brings a verse from יחזקאל showing that the key of תחיית המתים is in ה׳'s hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...to her, and He opened her womb.' And from where do we know that the key of תחיית המתים is in ה׳'s hand? As it is written: 'And you shall know that I am ה׳ when I open your graves.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is going through רבי יוחנן's list of keys ה׳ keeps for Himself, bringing a verse for each one. Here it finishes the childbirth verse and proves the key of תחיית המתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each key is proven from a verse that uses the root 'open' (פתח) about ה׳ Himself. For childbirth ה׳ 'opened her womb,' and for תחיית המתים ה׳ says 'when I open your graves.' Because ה׳ does the opening Himself, the key is not handed to a messenger.

keyTerms.meaning: A key; here, a power that ה׳ keeps for Himself
Bringing the dead back to life
From where do we know?
As it is written

phrases.english: to her, and He opened her womb.
phrases.notes: This finishes בראשית 30:22, the proof for the key of childbirth. The פסוק started on the previous page.

phrases.english: From where do we know the key of the resurrection of the dead?
As it is written:
And you shall know that I am ה׳
when I open your graves.
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 37:13

steps.triggerLanguage: מַפְתֵּחַ שֶׁל תְּחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים מִנַּיִן

steps.title: The scholars of ארץ ישראל add a key of פרנסה
steps.stepSummary: The scholars in ארץ ישראל say there is another key in ה׳'s hand: the key of פרנסה. They prove it from the verse 'You open Your hand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they say: the key of פרנסה is also in ה׳'s hand, as it is written: 'You open Your hand, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: A different group of scholars adds a fourth key to רבי יוחנן's list of three: the key of פרנסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof follows the same pattern as before. The verse says ה׳ Himself 'opens' His hand to feed every living thing. That means feeding the world is also a key ה׳ keeps for Himself.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
They say
Livelihood, food and support

phrases.english: In the West they say:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which lies west of Bavel.

phrases.english: also the key of livelihood,
as it is written: 'You open Your hand, etc.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 145:16

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא אָמְרִי: אַף מַפְתֵּחַ שֶׁל פַּרְנָסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an extra key to the list just finished
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The key of פרנסה is also kept in ה׳'s hand

steps.title: Why did רבי יוחנן leave out livelihood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not count the key of פרנסה in his list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what is the reason he does not count this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן's list is missing the key of פרנסה, since it also has a verse behind it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a verse showing that ה׳ 'opens' for פרנסה too. So leaving it out looks like a gap in רבי יוחנן's list, and the גמרא wants to know how he would explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
He does not count

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan, what is the reason
that he does not count this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב לְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי יוחנן's list in light of the added key
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן's list does not include the key of פרנסה

steps.title: Rain already counts as livelihood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן would answer that rain is the same thing as פרנסה, so the key of rain already covers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: rain is the same as פרנסה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן. He did not leave פרנסה out; it is already included in the key of גשמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All food and livelihood depend on rain. So the key of גשמים, which is already on רבי יוחנן's list, covers פרנסה too. The two lists do not really disagree; one simply names פרנסה separately.

keyTerms.meaning: He would tell you
Rain
Is the same as

steps.whatToRemember: There are three keys ה׳ keeps for Himself: childbirth, תחיית המתים, and rain. Rain also covers פרנסה.

phrases.english: He would tell you:
Rain is the same as livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: גְּשָׁמִים הַיְינוּ פַּרְנָסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Inclusion: the missing item is already contained in an item on the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן left out a key that has its own verse
steps.terutzMaskana: פרנסה is included within the key of גשמים

steps.title: Where does רבי אליעזר learn his starting date for mentioning rain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר in the משנה, who says we start mentioning rain from the first יום טוב of סוכות. It then asks where he learns this: from לולב or from ניסוך המים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: from the first יום טוב of the festival, etc. It was asked: from where does רבי אליעזר learn it? Does he learn it from לולב, or does he learn it from ניסוך המים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks what source רבי אליעזר used for starting the mention of rain on the first day of סוכות. It offers two choices, and the next steps explain why the choice matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both לולב and ניסוך המים are סוכות מצוות connected to rain, so either one could be the source. The question is not just about the source; each choice leads to a different starting time, as the next steps show.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them; a question the scholars were unsure about
He learns it
The palm branch taken on סוכות
Pouring water on the מזבח on סוכות

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: מִיּוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: From the first Yom Tov of the festival, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. 'The festival' means סוכות, and the topic is when we start mentioning rain in davening.

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
From where does Rabbi Eliezer learn it?
Does he learn it from the lulav,
or does he learn it from the water libation?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מֵהֵיכָא גָּמַיר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to רבי אליעזר's opinion in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר's source is לולב or ניסוך המים

steps.title: If the source is לולב, mentioning rain starts by day
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר learns from לולב, the mention of rain starts during the day, because לולב is a daytime מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he learns it from לולב: just as לולב is by day, so too the mention of rain is by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the first side of the question. If לולב is the source, the mention of rain begins only during the day of the first יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לולב is taken only in the daytime. If the mention of rain is modeled on לולב, it follows the same timing, so we would not mention rain at מעריב on the night of יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... so too; the form of a comparison
Mentioning rain (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם)
By day

phrases.english: If he learns it from the lulav:
just as lulav is by day,
so too the mention is by day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִלּוּלָב גָּמַר לַהּ: מָה לוּלָב בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of the first side of the question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical result if לולב is the source: the mention starts by day

steps.title: If the source is the water libation, mentioning rain starts the night before
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר learns from ניסוך המים, the mention starts at night. The water pouring can be done from the night before, as learned from the verse 'and their meal offerings and their libations,' which allows them even at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps he learns it from ניסוך המים: just as ניסוך המים can be done from the night before, as the Master said, 'and their meal offerings and their libations' teaches that they may be brought even at night, so too the mention of rain starts from the night before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the second side of the question. If ניסוך המים is the source, the mention of rain starts already at night, at מעריב of the first יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teaching from the verse 'and their meal offerings and their libations' shows that libations may be brought even at night. So the water pouring can start the night before. If the mention of rain is modeled on it, the mention begins at night too. That is the practical difference between the two possible sources.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps
From the night before
As the Master said; quoting an earlier teaching
Their libations

steps.whatToRemember: The question of where רבי אליעזר learns from is really a question about timing. If from לולב, we start by day; if from ניסוך המים, we start the night before.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא מִנִּיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם גָּמַר לַהּ:
phrases.english: Or perhaps he learns it from the water libation:
just as the water libation is from the night before,
as the Master said:
'And their meal offerings and their libations' — even at night;
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:18

phrases.english: so too the mention is from the night before.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא מִנִּיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם גָּמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question, which leads to a different starting time
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical result if ניסוך המים is the source: the mention starts the night before

steps.title: רבי אבהו: רבי אליעזר learned it from the לולב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its question with a statement of רבי אבהו: רבי אליעזר learned his rule only from לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אבהו said, רבי אליעזר learned this only from the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from Steps 5–7: does רבי אליעזר learn from לולב or from ניסוך המים? רבי אבהו says it is from לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6 and 7 showed that the source makes a difference. לולב means the mention of rain starts during the day, and ניסוך המים would mean it starts at night. Since רבי אבהו says the source is לולב, according to רבי אליעזר we start mentioning rain in the daytime of the first day of סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to answer a question
He did not learn it (except from...)
The palm branch and the other species taken on סוכות

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for Rabbi Abbahu said:
Rabbi Eliezer did not learn it
except from the lulav.
phrases.notes: So the mention of rain starts in the daytime, since that is when the לולב is taken (Step 6).

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Steps 5–7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר learns from לולב or from ניסוך המים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From לולב only, so the mention of rain begins during the day.

steps.title: How רבי אבהו knew this
steps.stepSummary: There are two versions of how רבי אבהו knew this: from a tradition he received, or from a ברייתא he heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי אבהו had this as a tradition passed down to him. Others say he heard it from a ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי אבהו got his information. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא shows the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו is reporting something, not making it up. One view says he received it as a passed-down tradition. The other says he figured it out from a ברייתא, and the גמרא will now quote that ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces another version
He received it as a tradition from his teachers
A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: Some say:
Rabbi Abbahu learned it as a tradition,
phrases.notes: Here גמרא means a teaching passed down from teacher to student, not the book of גמרא.

phrases.english: and some say:
he heard it from a baraita.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ גְּמָרָא גְּמִיר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains where רבי אבהו's statement in Step 8 comes from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two versions: רבי אבהו knew it from a tradition, or he heard it from a ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא: from taking the לולב or from putting it down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says we mention rain from when the לולב is taken, and רבי יהושע says from when it is put down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which ברייתא is it? It was taught: From when do we mention rain? רבי אליעזר says: from when the לולב is taken. רבי יהושע says: from when it is put down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which ברייתא רבי אבהו heard, and then quotes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, רבי אליעזר ties the start of mentioning rain directly to taking the לולב. That is exactly רבי אבהו's point: the source is the לולב. רבי יהושע ties it to putting the לולב down, which is at the end of סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? Asks which source is meant
As was taught in a ברייתא
Taking the לולב, starting on the first day of סוכות
Putting it down, when we stop taking the לולב at the end of סוכות

phrases.english: What is it? As it was taught:
From when do we mention the rains?
Rabbi Eliezer says:
From the time of taking the lulav.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
From the time of putting it down.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הִיא — דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the ברייתא mentioned in the second version of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says rain is mentioned from the taking of the לולב.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reason: the four species are about water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains that the four species are brought to ask for favor about water. Just as they cannot exist without water, the world cannot exist without water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: These four species come only to ask for God's favor about water. Just as these four species cannot exist without water, so the world cannot exist without water.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי אליעזר's reason for starting to mention rain when the לולב is taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four species all need water to grow, so taking them is a kind of request for water. Since the world also depends on water, it fits to start mentioning rain when we take them.

keyTerms.meaning: The four species: לולב, אתרוג, הדס, ערבה
To ask for God's favor about water
Since

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
Since these four species

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָן בָּאִין אֶלָּא לְרַצּוֹת עַל הַמַּיִם,
phrases.english: come only to ask for favor about the water,
and just as these four species
cannot exist without water,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא מַיִם.
phrases.english: so the world cannot exist without water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: הוֹאִיל וְאַרְבַּעַת מִינִין הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי אליעזר's position in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is mentioned from the taking of the לולב, because the four species are about water.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows clearly that רבי אליעזר's source is the לולב. That is exactly what רבי אבהו said in Step 8.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: rain on סוכות is a bad sign
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע challenges רבי אליעזר: rain during סוכות is a sign of a curse, so why bring it up then?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: But rain during the festival is nothing but a sign of a curse!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע attacks רבי אליעזר's view. Rain on סוכות is bad, so it seems wrong to talk about rain then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain on סוכות stops people from sitting in the סוכה, so it is a bad sign. If so, how can we bring up rain in our prayers right at the start of the חג?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so...? Opens a challenge
During the festival, meaning סוכות
A sign of a curse

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
But rain during the festival
is nothing but a sign of a curse!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וַהֲלֹא גְּשָׁמִים בֶּחָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's reasoning in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's rule that we start mentioning rain from the first day of סוכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rain on סוכות is a curse, so it makes no sense to bring up rain during the חג.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: mentioning is not asking
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that he only means to mention rain, as praise of God, not to ask for it. It is like mentioning תחיית המתים all year. So one may mention rain all year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: I also did not say to ask for rain, only to mention it. Just as we mention תחיית המתים all year, even though it only comes in its time, so we mention the power of rain all year, even though rain only comes in its season. So if someone wants to mention rain all year, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers רבי יהושע's challenge. He separates asking for rain from mentioning rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking for rain now would be asking for a curse. But mentioning rain is only praising God's power, which does not ask for rain to fall right now. That is why one may even mention rain all year round.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask, meaning to request rain
To mention, meaning to praise God as the One who brings rain
The revival of the dead
The power of rain: God's might shown through rain

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'mentioning' (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם, praise) with 'asking' (ותן טל ומטר, a request). רבי אליעזר only allows mentioning during סוכות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
I too did not say to ask,
but only to mention.
And just as the revival of the dead
one mentions the entire year,
yet it comes only in its time,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ מַזְכִּירִין גְּבוּרוֹת גְּשָׁמִים כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: so we mention the power of rain all year,
yet they come only in their season.
Therefore, if one comes to mention
the entire year, he may mention.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי לִשְׁאוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's challenge from Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction: mentioning rain is different from asking for it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning rain on סוכות seemed like asking for a curse.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mentioning is only praise of God's power, like תחיית המתים, so it may be said even all year.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between mentioning rain and asking for rain is a basic idea behind the whole topic of when we add rain to תפילה.

steps.title: רבי: stop mentioning when you stop asking
steps.stepSummary: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) says that the time we stop asking for rain is also the time we stop mentioning it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: I say, from the time one stops asking for rain, one also stops mentioning it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a third opinion, from רבי, about when to stop mentioning rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said one may mention rain all year. רבי disagrees: mentioning rain is tied to asking for it, so both stop at the same time. This deals with when we stop mentioning rain, not when we start.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה
Stops
Asking: the request for rain
Mentioning: the praise of rain

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו says רבי אליעזר learned his rule from לולב, so according to רבי אליעזר we start mentioning rain in the daytime. In the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר explains that mentioning rain is praise, not a request, so it is fine on סוכות. רבי holds that mentioning rain and asking for it stop together.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: I say:
from the time one stops asking,
so one stops mentioning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר, אוֹמֵר אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אליעזר's statement in Step 13 that one may mention rain all year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mentioning rain stops at the same time as asking for rain.

steps.title: Two more opinions: the second day or the sixth day of סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי יהודה בן בתירה says we start mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות. רבי עקיבא says we start on the sixth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירה says: on the second day of the חג, one mentions rain. רבי עקיבא says: on the sixth day of the חג, one mentions rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps listing opinions about when we begin to mention rain in davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי אליעזר said to start when the לולב is taken, and רבי יהושע said to start when it is put down. Now we get two in-between opinions: the second day of the חג and the sixth day of the חג. The גמרא explains the reasons for these days later, in Steps 20–27.

keyTerms.meaning: He mentions (rain, in the second ברכה of שמונה עשרה)
On the חג, meaning סוכות
On the second day
On the sixth day

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
On the second day of the festival, one mentions rain,
Rabbi Akiva says:
On the sixth day of the festival, one mentions rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר: בַּשֵּׁנִי בֶּחָג הוּא מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of opinions in the ברייתא that was opened in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה בן בתירה: start mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות. רבי עקיבא: start on the sixth day.

steps.title: Which prayer leader mentions rain on שמיני עצרת and on the first day of פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה, quoting רבי יהושע, says that on שמיני עצרת the later prayer leader mentions rain and the first one does not. On the first day of פסח, the first prayer leader mentions rain and the later one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי יהושע: about the one who leads the davening on the last יום טוב of the חג, the last leader mentions rain and the first one does not. On the first יום טוב of פסח, the first leader mentions rain and the last one does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives one more opinion, which sets the exact starting point and stopping point by the prayer leaders of one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two leaders that day: the first leads שחרית and the last leads מוסף. On שמיני עצרת, we start mentioning rain at מוסף, so the שחרית leader does not mention it. On the first day of פסח it is the reverse: the שחרית leader still mentions rain, and we stop at מוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who passes before the ark, meaning the חזן or prayer leader
The last יום טוב of סוכות, meaning שמיני עצרת
The first leader, for שחרית
The last leader, for מוסף

steps.confusionAlert: "First" and "last" here do not mean the first day and the last day. They mean the first prayer leader (שחרית) and the later prayer leader (מוסף) on that same day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practice we keep today: we start mentioning rain at מוסף of שמיני עצרת and stop at מוסף of the first day of פסח.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
The one who passes before the ark
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא says "the חזן": the person who leads the davening.

phrases.english: on the last Festival day of the festival,
phrases.notes: This means שמיני עצרת.

phrases.english: the last one mentions rain,
the first one does not mention it.
On the first Festival day of Passover,
the first one mentions rain,
the last one does not mention it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final opinion in the ברייתא's list of when to start, and adds when to stop.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Start mentioning rain with the מוסף leader of שמיני עצרת. Stop with the מוסף leader of the first day of פסח.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's argument seems strong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רבי אליעזר answered רבי יהושע well. So how could רבי יהושע disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר spoke well to רבי יהושע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the argument from steps 12–13 and points out that רבי אליעזר's answer seems very good. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains how רבי יהושע would respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said that we only mention rain as praise of ה׳, the same way we mention תחיית המתים all year. If that is right, רבי יהושע's complaint that rain on סוכות is a curse seems to fall away. So why does רבי יהושע still hold his opinion?

keyTerms.meaning: He spoke well to him, meaning his argument is convincing

phrases.english: Well did he say to him,
Rabbi Eliezer to Rabbi Yehoshua!
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי אליעזר's answer: we only mention rain as praise, like תחיית המתים.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the list of opinions to the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's opinion, which does not start mentioning rain when the לולב is taken
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If mentioning rain is only praise, like תחיית המתים, then there should be no problem with mentioning it on סוכות or even all year.

steps.title: Every day is a fitting time for תחיית המתים, but not for rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע would answer: we mention תחיית המתים every day because any day is a fitting time for it. Rain, though, is not good at every time it falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע could say to you: it is fine to mention תחיית המתים, because every day is its time. But rain — is every time it comes its proper time?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהושע by showing that rain and תחיית המתים are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praising ה׳ for something only makes sense at a time when that thing is a blessing. תחיית המתים would be good on any day, so we can praise it all year. Rain is good only in its season, so we should not praise it at a time when it would be a curse.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you, meaning this is how he would answer
It makes sense with, meaning granted in that case
Bringing the dead back to life
Its proper time

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua could say to you:
Granted, one mentions the resurrection of the dead,
because every day is its proper time.
But rain,
is every time that it comes its proper time?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: בִּשְׁלָמָא תְּחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 for רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rain is just like תחיית המתים, so it can be praised at any time.
steps.terutzMaskana: תחיית המתים is fitting on any day, but rain is fitting only in its season, so we may not praise it out of season.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה: rain after ניסן is a curse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that rain out of season is bad. A משנה teaches that rain after ניסן is a sign of a curse, based on a פסוק about the wheat harvest.
steps.simpleTranslation: And didn't we learn in a משנה: if ניסן has passed and rain falls, it is a sign of a curse, as it says: "Is it not the wheat harvest today?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove the point from step 18: rain at the wrong time is not a blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes שמואל calling for rain during the wheat harvest as a punishment. So rain at harvest time is a curse. This shows clearly that rain is not good at all times, so it cannot be praised all year the way תחיית המתים is.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה
A sign of a curse
The wheat harvest

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's point: we praise ה׳ for rain only when rain is a blessing. Rain out of season, like after ניסן or during סוכות, is a sign of a curse.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:
If Nisan has passed and rain fell,
they are a sign of a curse,
as it is stated: "Is it not the wheat harvest today?" and so on.
phrases.notes: שמואל א 12:17. In that פסוק, rain at harvest time comes as a punishment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: יָצָא נִיסָן וְיָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the distinction in step 18 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That rain is not fitting at every time of year
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (later in this מסכתא) based on שמואל א 12:17: rain after ניסן is a sign of a curse

steps.title: What is the reason for רבי יהודה בן בתירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה בן בתירה's opinion, that we start mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות, and asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירה says: on the second day of the חג one mentions rain. What is the reason of רבי יהודה בן בתירה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה בן בתירה's line from the ברייתא again so it can start a new topic: finding the source for his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why the second day, and not the first day or the last day? The גמרא wants to find the reason behind this specific day. This opens a new section of the discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
On the second day of the festival, one mentions rain.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argument and opens an explanation of the opinion from step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reason for starting to mention rain on the second day of סוכות

steps.title: The answer begins: a ברייתא from רבי יהודה בן בתירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer by bringing another ברייתא where רבי יהודה בן בתירה speaks. His actual words come in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה בן בתירה says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its answer by opening a ברייתא. This line only sets up the next move, because רבי יהודה בן בתירה's actual words come right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for his opinion will come from a different teaching of his own. In that teaching he finds a hint to the water pouring on סוכות in the פסוקים about the offerings. The next step gives that teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a ברייתא of רבי יהודה בן בתירה himself. Its content is given in Step 22.

steps.title: Three extra letters spell 'water'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירה points to three words in the סוכות offering פסוקים whose extra letters spell מים. This is a hint in the תורה to ניסוך המים.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the second day the פסוק says 'and their libations,' on the sixth day it says 'and its libations,' and on the seventh day it says 'according to their laws.' Together that gives מ, י, מ, which spells מים, 'water.' From here we have a hint in the תורה to the water pouring.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 21 continues. רבי יהודה בן בתירה shows where the תורה hints at pouring water on the מזבח during סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the other days the פסוקים use a shorter wording. On these three days each word has one extra letter: a ם in ונסכיהם, a י in ונסכיה, and a ם in כמשפטם. Put together, the letters spell מים, so the תורה is hinting at ניסוך המים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And their libations': the second-day word, with an extra ם
'And its libations': the sixth-day word, with an extra י
'According to their laws': the seventh-day word, with an extra ם
A hint, not a clear, open statement
Pouring water on the מזבח during סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: The extra letters do not come one after another in a single פסוק. Each one comes from a different day: the second, the sixth, and the seventh.
steps.whyThisMatters: This hint is the foundation for both opinions that follow. Each one ties the start of mentioning rain to the day the hint begins.

phrases.english: It is stated on the second day: "and their libations,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:19. Watch for the extra ם at the end of the word.

phrases.english: and it is stated on the sixth day: "and its libations,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:31. Here the extra letter is the י.

phrases.english: and it is stated on the seventh day: "according to their laws."
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:33. On the other days it just says כמשפט, so the ם here is extra.

phrases.english: Here we have mem, yud, mem,
so here we have "water."

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן רֶמֶז לְנִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: From here there is a hint in the Torah to the water pouring.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר בַּשֵּׁנִי ״וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that Step 21 began quoting.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra letters מ־י־מ in the second, sixth and seventh day פסוקים spell מים, a hint to ניסוך המים.

steps.title: Why start on the second day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה בן בתירה picked the second day to start mentioning rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about the second day, that he chose it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the hint we just learned. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hint is spread over three days: the second, sixth and seventh. So why should mentioning rain begin on the second day, and not on one of the others?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this and not something else?
He took, he chose

phrases.english: And what is different about the second day, that he chose it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא בְּשֵׁנִי דְּנָקֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the hint from Step 22 leads to the second day in particular.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the second day was chosen when the hint is spread over three days.

steps.title: The hint begins on the second day
steps.stepSummary: The first time the פסוק hints at the water is on the second day, so that is when we start mentioning rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק hints at the water, the hint starts on the second day. So we mention rain from the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 23. We start where the hint starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first letter of מים appears in the second-day word ונסכיהם. Since the hint to the water begins there, mentioning rain also begins there.

keyTerms.meaning: They are hinted at
Therefore
We mention (rain in the תפילה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה בן בתירה: the hint to ניסוך המים starts on the second day of סוכות, so we start mentioning rain on the second day.

phrases.english: Because when the verse hints at them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the water pourings.

phrases.english: it is on the second day that it hints at them;
therefore we mention rain from the second day.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי רְמִיזִי לְהוּ בִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hint first appears on the second day, so mentioning rain starts then.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: start on the sixth day
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says we start mentioning rain on the sixth day of סוכות. The plural word there, 'and its libations,' points to two pourings: water and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: one starts mentioning rain on the sixth day of the festival. On the sixth day the פסוק says 'and its libations,' in the plural, so it is speaking of two pourings: one of water and one of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי עקיבא's opinion from the ברייתא (Step 15), that we start mentioning rain on the sixth day, and explains his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא focuses on the sixth-day word: the plural 'libations' means two pourings. One is the usual wine and the other is water, so for him the hint to the water begins on the sixth day. Step 27 shows that he still relies on רבי יהודה בן בתירה's idea that water is hinted in these פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: On the sixth day of the festival (סוכות)
The פסוק is speaking about
The regular wine pouring that comes with the offerings

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions tie mentioning rain to the day the hint to ניסוך המים begins. רבי יהודה בן בתירה says the second day (from the three letters), and רבי עקיבא says the sixth day (from the plural ונסכיה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
On the sixth day of the festival one mentions rain,
as it is stated on the sixth day: "and its libations";
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:31. This is the same word from Step 22.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking of two pourings:
one is the water pouring,
and one is the wine pouring.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: בַּשִּׁשִּׁי בֶּחָג הוּא מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי יהודה בן בתירה's opinion, the גמרא now explains רבי עקיבא's opinion from Step 15, which has a different starting day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mentioning rain begins on the sixth day of סוכות, because the plural ונסכיה hints at both the water and the wine pourings.

steps.title: Maybe both libations are wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא: the plural 'its libations' could mean two wine pourings, not water and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that both pourings are of wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי עקיבא's reading from the step before. Two libations does not prove that one of them is water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said the plural word 'and its libations' means two pourings: water and wine. The challenge says the plural only proves there are two pourings, and both could be wine. If so, there is no hint to ניסוך המים here, and no reason to start mentioning rain on the sixth day.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / I could say (offering another way to read it)
Both of them
Wine

phrases.english: Say that both of them are of wine!
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means the two pourings רבי עקיבא learned from the plural 'and its libations.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא תַּרְוַיְיהוּ דְּחַמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's reading of the plural 'and its libations' from Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's claim that the plural 'and its libations' means one water pouring and one wine pouring.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plural word only shows there are two pourings. It does not show what liquid is poured, so both could be wine.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא agrees the פסוקים hint at water
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds like רבי יהודה בן בתירה, who showed that the extra letters in the פסוקים hint at water, so the second pouring must be water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי יהודה בן בתירה, who said: water is hinted at.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי עקיבא already accepts that the תורה hints at a water pouring, so the extra pouring he finds on the sixth day is the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא uses רבי יהודה בן בתירה's idea from Step 22, that extra letters in the סוכות פסוקים spell מים. Since water is already hinted in the תורה, the plural word on the sixth day shows where that water pouring belongs. So the two pourings are water and wine, not two of wine.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (he agrees with the opinion of)
They are hinted at
Water

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה בן בתירה both agree the תורה hints at ניסוך המים. They argue only about which day the hint begins: the second day or the sixth day. That decides when we start mentioning rain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows רבי עקיבא's source depends on רבי יהודה בן בתירה's hint. The two opinions share one idea and differ only about where in the פסוקים the water shows up.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה,
phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: who said: water is hinted at.
phrases.notes: This points back to the extra letters that spell מים (Step 22).

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 26 by tying רבי עקיבא to רבי יהודה בן בתירה's hint from Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking to another opinion: רבי עקיבא accepts an earlier source that settles the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural 'and its libations' could mean two pourings of wine, so there would be no water hint on the sixth day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the פסוקים already hint at water, one of the two pourings on the sixth day is water and the other is wine.
